title: Sicilian Anchovy Broccolini Tray
seoTitle: Sicilian Anchovy Broccolini Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Charred broccolini tray—lemon garlic finish, green side that actually tastes grilled
subtitle: Grilled broccolini, lemon-garlic oil, and parmesan tray for ten
description: Broccolini bundles toss in olive oil, grill until charred and tender, and finish with lemon-garlic oil, parmesan, and chili flakes on a big tray for ten.

steps.title: Prep broccolini
steps.instruction: Trim tough ends. Toss broccolini with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use anchovy fillets, golden raisins, pine nuts, Pecorino Romano as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Build lemon-garlic oil
steps.instruction: Warm olive oil with garlic 2 minutes off heat. Add lemon zest and juice. Reserve for service. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 425°F. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill in batches
steps.instruction: Grill broccolini in basket, turning, until charred and tender, 6–8 minutes per batch. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F for any egg-based components on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold wrapped
steps.instruction: Transfer to hotel pan, cover with foil, hold at 170°F up to 25 minutes. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Lemon oil finish
steps.instruction: Drizzle lemon-garlic oil over broccolini at service—not before long hold. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Parmesan and chili
steps.instruction: Grate parmesan and scatter chili flakes over tray at the line. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tray for ten
steps.instruction: Spread charred broccolini in a hotel pan for buffet-style service alongside mains. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Grill basket keeps thin broccolini stems from falling through grates.
Charred tips and tender stems are the goal—don't overcook to mush.
Lemon oil at the line keeps broccolini glossy; added early gets soggy.
tonightSpread: Charred broccolini lemon tray with parmesan.
Complements steak, chicken, or seafood mains.
leftovers: Chop into frittata or omelet filling.
Toss into pasta with extra lemon and parmesan.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Broccolini grills faster than broccoli crowns and looks sharp on the line. Holds at 170°F wrapped in foil and pairs with any protein.
mealPrepNotes: Grill broccolini medium-high 425°F in batches, 6–8 minutes. Hold wrapped at 170°F up to 25 minutes. Lemon oil and parmesan at service.
